macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global markets whipsawed by renewed U.S.-Iran tensions and surging oil
items.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. stock futures, European shares, and Asian equities were shaped by renewed Middle East conflict, while oil prices jumped and bonds sold off as investors reassessed inflation and supply risks. The coverage also noted firmer safe-haven demand for the dollar and a jump in Japan’s 10-year government bond yield to a 30-year high.

items.title: IMF cuts 2026 global growth forecast after Iran war fallout
items.summary: Al Jazeera reported that the IMF lowered its 2026 world growth outlook to 3% and linked the downgrade to the economic fallout from the Iran conflict. The report said AI-related demand partly offset the energy shock, but higher oil prices still pressured travel and other fuel-sensitive sectors.

items.title: Fed officials signal concern about inflation, leaving rate path uncertain
items.summary: The Financial Times reported that some Federal Reserve officials saw a need for future rate increases to contain inflation. That reinforced market attention on the Fed’s next move as inflation-sensitive assets and Treasury yields remained volatile.

items.title: U.S. labor and housing data show a mixed macro backdrop
items.summary: Investing.com’s economic calendar showed initial jobless claims at 215,000, continuing claims at 1.814 million, and existing home sales at 4.09 million, alongside a speech from FOMC member Williams. The same calendar highlighted upcoming high-impact events such as central bank decisions, GDP, CPI, and unemployment data.

items.title: PepsiCo tops revenue expectations as consumers tighten spending
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reported that PepsiCo posted stronger-than-expected second-quarter revenue despite weaker demand in North America. The company said consumers were tightening budgets because of broader economic concerns.

items.title: Travel and oil-sensitive stocks move on crude spike after ceasefire collapse
items.summary: Yahoo Finance said crude oil rose sharply after the ceasefire broke, with WTI and gasoline futures both posting strong gains. The report noted that travel stocks were hit while energy shares benefited from the move.

items.title: Chip stocks rebound in premarket trading
items.summary: CNBC reported that chip stocks were jumping again in premarket trading, alongside notable moves in names such as AstraZeneca, PepsiCo, Salesforce, and Levi. The report pointed to another volatile session for equity leadership groups.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin slides below $64,000 as weak demand and risk appetite weigh on crypto markets
items.summary: Bitcoin fell about 2% to 2.3% in the past 24 hours, briefly slipping below $64,000 and trading near $63,800 to $63,900 as stablecoin inflows weakened and broader risk sentiment stayed fragile. Ether also underperformed, with multiple market trackers reporting declines across major crypto assets.

items.title: U.S. crypto market structure bill faces fresh setbacks in the Senate
items.summary: The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act is still struggling to secure enough Senate support, with Democrats objecting to ethics provisions tied to President Trump's crypto interests. Senate Majority Leader John Thune said passage before the summer recess was unlikely.

items.title: EU reportedly preparing to reopen MiCA rulebook for non-EU stablecoin issuers
items.summary: European Union diplomats told Euronews that the bloc is preparing to revisit its Markets in Crypto-Assets framework, potentially in 2027, to tighten rules for stablecoin issuers outside the EU. The move would add another layer of regulatory scrutiny to the global stablecoin market.

items.title: Gate says customer external information may have been leaked in recent security incident
items.summary: Gate issued a response to a recent security event, saying customer external information was exposed and that it had begun tracing the flow of funds. The disclosure adds to concerns about exchange security and operational risk in the sector.

items.title: BlackRock reportedly moves $256.8 million in BTC and ETH to Coinbase
items.summary: Odaily reported that BlackRock deposited a combined $256.8 million worth of Bitcoin and Ether to Coinbase over the past 24 hours. The transfer stood out as one of the larger notable institutional blockchain transactions in the day’s news flow.

items.title: MARA acquires majority stake in Texas 2,000 MW computing-campus project
items.summary: MARA said it will spend up to $600 million to acquire a majority stake in a Texas project company tied to a 2,000 MW compute campus. The deal underscores continued expansion in Bitcoin mining infrastructure and energy-intensive data-center development.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work for workplace automation
items.summary: OpenAI unveiled ChatGPT Work, an agent designed to execute tasks across different applications and files, expanding its push into professional AI tools. The release intensifies competition with Anthropic and other enterprise AI providers.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-Live voice models for real-time conversation
items.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-Live, a new family of voice models that can listen and speak simultaneously in real time. The company says the capability is aimed at more natural live conversation and translation use cases.

items.title: Meta opens developer access to Muse Spark 1.1
items.summary: Meta released developer access to its Muse Spark AI model and an upgraded version, positioning it more directly against paid AI offerings from Anthropic and OpenAI. The move broadens access to Meta’s latest model line.

items.title: SpaceXAI launches Grok 4.5 for coding and agentic tasks
items.summary: SpaceXAI released Grok 4.5, which it described as its most intelligent model to date. The company says the model is designed for coding and agentic tasks.

items.title: U.S. lifts restrictions on Anthropic’s latest Claude models
items.summary: The Trump administration lifted restrictions on Anthropic’s latest versions of its Claude chatbot after a cybersecurity-related pause. Reuters reported the move as part of a broader reassessment of access to advanced AI systems.

items.title: Anthropic appoints Ben Bernanke to Long-Term Benefit Trust
items.summary: Anthropic said it appointed former U.S. Federal Reserve chair Ben Bernanke to its Long-Term Benefit Trust, an oversight body tasked with ensuring the company stays aligned with its public mission. The appointment adds a high-profile governance figure to Anthropic’s structure.

items.title: Meta plans to begin manufacturing an AI chip in September
items.summary: Reuters reported that Meta plans to start manufacturing an artificial intelligence chip from September, according to an internal memo. The company is also targeting major expansion in computing power to support its AI efforts.

items.title: Micron announces more than $250 billion U.S. investment through 2035
items.summary: Micron said it plans to invest more than $250 billion in the United States through 2035, citing surging demand for memory chips in the AI era. The announcement underscores continued infrastructure spending tied to AI growth.

items.title: Meta to build first Canadian data center in Alberta
items.summary: Meta announced it will build a massive data center in central Alberta, its first in Canada. The project reflects the company’s ongoing expansion of compute infrastructure for AI workloads.

items.title: OpenAI faces new copyright sanctions motion in ChatGPT lawsuit
items.summary: The New York Times and other news publishers filed a new motion accusing OpenAI of hiding tools and datasets that could identify copyrighted journalism in ChatGPT outputs. The filing escalates the broader copyright dispute around generative AI training and outputs.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Microsoft gaming cuts deepen, with studio closures and layoffs reported
items.summary: Reports from the past day say Xbox has cut jobs across multiple teams, including the closure of an IO Interactive studio and major restructuring that has affected several studios. The Verge also reports Microsoft is selling off four Xbox studios as part of broader gaming cuts.

items.title: Capcom moves up Onimusha: Way of the Sword release date
items.summary: Capcom has advanced the launch of Onimusha: Way of the Sword to September 4, earlier than its previously planned September 25 release. This is one of the biggest release-date changes in the latest wave of game news.

items.title: Nintendo confirms Mario Kart Tour shutdown
items.summary: Nintendo has confirmed that Mario Kart Tour will be shut down this September after seven years of service, and there will be no offline version. The announcement marks another major mobile-game sunset from Nintendo.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced launches on consoles
items.summary: A restored version of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced went live on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, with the PC release following later due to Steam timing differences. Early reports say the game has already posted a strong Steam player peak.

items.title: DOOM: The Dark Ages gets story DLC update
items.summary: Developers have released a narrative expansion for DOOM: The Dark Ages, bringing paid content and a major update to PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and PC. It is one of the main game content drops mentioned in current industry coverage.

items.title: Pokémon GO holds 10th anniversary live event
items.summary: Pokémon GO marked its 10th anniversary with a special livestream featuring announcements and surprises. Coverage indicates the event included live reveals tied to the mobile game’s milestone.

items.title: GTA Online’s next big update announced for next week
items.summary: Rockstar’s next GTA Online update, The Kortz Center Heist, is scheduled for release next week. Fans have already found Rockstar-related Easter eggs in the lead-up.

items.title: Nintendo expands classic game catalog with more retro titles
items.summary: IGN reports that Nintendo added Wario Land: Super Mario Land 3 to its classic game catalog, alongside additional retro titles from the Game Boy and Game Boy Advance libraries. This continues Nintendo’s ongoing retro library rollout.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Swift launches blockchain-based shared ledger with 16 banks
items.summary: Swift unveiled a blockchain-based shared ledger with an initial group of 16 banks, including Citi and HSBC, to enable around-the-clock payments and compete with stablecoin-driven payment systems.

items.title: India removes import duties on some electronics and smartphone parts
items.summary: India scrapped import duties on selected mobile phone and electronics components, a move that could lower costs for manufacturers such as Apple and Xiaomi.

items.title: Apple to spend more than $30 billion under Broadcom chip-supply agreement
items.summary: Apple said it will spend more than $30 billion as part of a chip-supply agreement with Broadcom, which will also expand a factory in Colorado.

items.title: Meta plans in-house manufacturing for new AI glasses
items.summary: Meta announced a new line of smart glasses designed in-house, signaling a deeper push into wearable tech and a more direct hardware strategy.

items.title: Microsoft lays off nearly 5,000 workers, most in Xbox division
items.summary: Microsoft is cutting about 3,200 jobs across its Xbox business as it restructures the division and reallocates resources toward artificial intelligence and broader business priorities.

items.title: South Korea plans $518 billion chip manufacturing hub investment
items.summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix plan to invest a combined $518 billion in a new chip manufacturing hub as part of a larger push tied to surging demand for advanced semiconductors.

items.title: EU backs temporary rules for scanning online child abuse material
items.summary: EU lawmakers supported a proposal to reinstate temporary rules that would let platforms such as Google and Meta detect and remove child sexual abuse material online.

items.title: SpaceX launches Gen 3 Starlink system for higher-capacity satellite internet
items.summary: SpaceX told the FCC that its Gen 3 Starlink system is intended to provide higher-capacity satellite internet for consumers and connected devices, with ultra low-latency and multi-gigabit speeds targeted.
